note: IMMUTABLE. v2 keeps v1's tasks and seed UNCHANGED and only raises the token budget 64000 -> 96000. Rationale: a budget ablation (re-thresholding a 128k run of minimax-m2.5 by per-item token usage, and 96k reruns of every model that truncated at 64k) showed the 64k cap was invalidly penalising verbose reasoners via truncation - e.g. Sonnet 4.6 went 16% -> 67% exact and minimax-m2.5 12% -> 24% purely from the budget change, with no other change. 96k captures essentially all reasoning (max output observed ~107k; only the most verbose models still truncate a few items). A budget change alters scores, so it is a NEW version, never an edit to v1. Scores are comparable within a version only.

official_run_config.tools: OFF (mandatory - with a code interpreter these tasks are trivial)
official_run_config.scoring: per-item conjunctive exact-match (headline) + per-row/per-part marginal accuracy (graded, primary); no LLM judge
official_run_config.validity_guard: only trust items with stop_reason == 'end_turn'. max_tokens = truncated, None = timeout - both invalid. Truncations are surfaced, never silently scored as wrong.

caveats: Cross-model panel measured (see docs/leaderboard.json): the top five are all Anthropic; open models top out at minimax-m2.5 (24% exact / 47% per-row).
Newer-is-not-always-better: Opus 4.6 (67% exact) and Sonnet 4.6 (67%) beat their newer siblings Opus 4.8 (58%) and Sonnet 5 (47%). Opus 4.6's LIFE result reproduced across two runs (92% / 88%).

Even at 96k the most verbose reasoners still truncate a few items (Sonnet 4.6 ~25, minimax-m2.5 ~4), so their true scores may be marginally higher. For the most verbose models there is no budget that is not somewhat unfair; truncation counts are reported for transparency.
Sample n=25 per task (100 items); ~+/-10% band, so close rankings (e.g. within the Anthropic cluster) are not statistically separable.
Domain is two cellular-automata families (faithful long-horizon simulation).
